accountNeeded: Google Cloud account with a Cloud project
agentCan: Draft consent screen text and privacy policy outline
approvalWait: Brand verification typically 2 to 3 business days if branding changed, sensitive scope verification can take up to around 10 days after a complete submission in some Google guidance, and restricted scope verification can take several weeks, plus a security assessment. Treat all of these as ranges, not guarantees.

blockers.blocker: Unverified app warning and 100 user cap
blockers.fix: Complete verification for production use. The warning and cap are expected in Testing mode for sensitive or restricted scopes.

blockers.blocker: Scope list in code does not match the consent screen declaration
blockers.fix: List every scope from code, then make the declaration match exactly. Trimming a scope from the declaration that code still requests will fail review.

blockers.blocker: Demo video does not show a scope in use
blockers.fix: Re-record with that exact feature, with the same app name and branding as the submission.

blockers.blocker: Restricted scope needs a security assessment
blockers.fix: Budget for assessment time and cost separately, and consider whether a narrower sensitive scope can ship first.

checklist.item: Cloud project and only the APIs you need are enabled
Consent screen branding matches the real app exactly
Privacy policy and homepage URLs are live and accurate
Redirect URIs match the code exactly
Every scope classified as non-sensitive, sensitive, or restricted
Scope justifications written for each sensitive or restricted scope
Demo video shows the full consent flow and each scope in use
Test users added and full flow tested in Testing mode
Third party security assessment planned, for restricted scopes with server access

consoleName: Google Cloud Console, APIs and Services, OAuth consent screen
cost: Free to register. A third party security assessment for restricted scopes can be paid, amount varies by assessor and is not stated here.
difficultyWhy: Basic setup is fast, but sensitive and restricted scopes trigger verification, a demo video, and in restricted cases a third party security assessment.
humanMust: Create the Cloud project and consent screen
Book and complete a security assessment if required
managedAppNote: If a managed directory already covers the Google scopes you need, use it for a first version. Register your own app when you need your own branding, client ID, or restricted scopes.
name: Google

setupTime: 2 to 4 hours for basic setup, plus 1 to 3 days to prepare a clean verification submission

steps.blockerTip: Enabling every Google API at once makes scope review harder later. Enable only what the feature uses.
steps.detail: Create a project, enable only the APIs your agent will call, for example Gmail, Drive, or Calendar APIs.
steps.title: Create a Cloud project and enable the APIs you need

steps.blockerTip: Branding mismatches are a common verification failure. The name, logo, and URLs on screen must match the real app.
steps.detail: Choose External for outside users or Internal for your own organization only. Add app name, support email, homepage, and privacy policy URLs that match the real app.
steps.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen

steps.blockerTip: Redirect URIs must match exactly. Test with the exact URI your code uses.
steps.detail: Create a Web application client, add your exact authorized redirect URIs, and store the client ID and secret securely.
steps.title: Create OAuth client credentials and redirect URIs

steps.blockerTip: Adding a new sensitive or restricted scope later requires a new verification request. Get the scope list right before you submit.
steps.detail: List every scope your code requests, then check Google's classification: non-sensitive, sensitive, or restricted. For example, full Gmail or Drive content is restricted, while some narrower scopes are sensitive. Do not request a broad scope if a narrower one works.
steps.title: Classify every scope before you request it

steps.blockerTip: Unverified apps show a warning and are capped at about 100 new users for sensitive or restricted scopes. That cap is a signal you still need verification for production.
steps.detail: In Testing mode, add test users, run the full consent flow, and confirm the consent screen shows the correct app name, scopes, and client ID in the browser address bar.
steps.title: Test in Testing mode with test users

steps.blockerTip: Record the video with the same app name and branding as the submission, and show each scope actually being used. A generic demo is a common rejection reason.
steps.detail: For sensitive scopes, prepare scope justifications, a demo video in English showing the full consent flow and the feature using each scope, and accurate branding. For restricted scopes, plan for a third party security assessment as well.
steps.title: Prepare the verification submission

steps.blockerTip: Changing scopes or consent screen branding after submission can require a new verification request. Freeze the scope list during review.
steps.detail: Submit for brand verification first if needed, then for scope verification. Answer reviewer questions quickly and with the exact scope list from your code.
steps.title: Submit and respond to reviewer questions
